title: Split by time and build features from the past
prompt:
The team will train on the past and test on the most recent months. If a feature has seen even one test rating, the test result looks better than the model really is. So the split is by time, at the fixed cutoff `CUTOFF` in your file, and the features use the training rows only.

Write `training_interactions(ratings)` and `evaluation_interactions(ratings)`, then `movie_features(ratings, movies)` and `user_features(ratings, users)` from the training rows. This step checks `movie_features`; the last step checks the rest.
rules: Training rows are rated before `CUTOFF`; evaluation rows on or after it. A rating exactly at the cutoff is an evaluation row.
Split the raw rows first, then clean each side with `clean_interactions`. A re-rating after the cutoff must not change or remove the training rating it replaces.

`movie_features` is your `movie_stats` built from the training rows only, and `user_features` is your `user_stats` built from them. A film or member whose ratings all come after the cutoff is a cold start.
hints: `ratings.filter(F.col("rated_at") < CUTOFF)` keeps the training rows. Pass that to `clean_interactions`, not the other way round.
Cleaning first would keep only a re-rating made after the cutoff, and the training rating it replaced would vanish from training.
`movie_stats` cleans whatever ratings it's given, and cleaning clean rows changes nothing. So `movie_stats(training_interactions(ratings), movies)` is the whole function.
explanation: A fixed cutoff makes the split the same on every run, unlike a random split, and it matches how the model will be used: trained on what's known, tested on what came later. Filtering the raw rows before cleaning is the subtle part. If you clean first, a member who re-rates a film after the cutoff loses their earlier training rating, because the later one wins and then lands in evaluation: the future has changed the training set. Splitting first keeps each side's latest rating within its own period. Building features through `movie_stats` and `user_stats` on the training rows means nothing from the evaluation months reaches them: a film first rated after the cutoff is a cold start, which is exactly what the model will face. The training rows feed several tables, so `cache()` on them would save work if they were used many times in one job.
